speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what are the top three ways by which the Ministry is alerted to potential kickback offences; (b) what are the respective percentages of cases that are reported via each of the top three ways by which the Ministry is alerted to kickback offences; and (c) how is the Ministry strengthening efforts to get workers to report kickback offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: MOM also educates first-time migrant workers on kickback offences and ways to seek help through the mandatory Settling-In Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: We have stepped up our engagement and education efforts by tapping on the network of migrant worker volunteers being developed by the Assurance, Care and Engagement (ACE) group and Migrant Workers' Centre (MWC) ambassadors to disseminate key employment messages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: MOM will continue to work with community partners, leverage technology, such as the FWMOMCare app, and tap on social media channels to amplify these messages and reach out to more migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know of migrant workers who paid over $10,000 in kickbacks to come to Singapore to work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think, no matter how good our labour laws are, this huge power imbalance and the fact that they are so heavily in debt would make our laws quite ineffective because not many would dare to speak up.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One, whether we can step up the protection for whistle-blowers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think the Senior Minister of State mentioned about helping them find employment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I think, in Taiwan, they go a step further by even providing financial incentives for those who reported the violations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Instead of focusing on giving financial incentives for people who are, especially migrant workers who come forward and make that complaint, it is more likely important to help them understand what exactly a kickback is.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Settling-In Programme is very important in helping them be aware what constitutes a kickback and then, to explain to them that, actually, they would be protected from loss of jobs should they report the employer for collecting illegal kickbacks.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think what they look for is more protection and job security and that is something that we want to provide.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think there are some proposals out there on whether we can do some accreditation of the recruiting agencies at where the kickbacks are paid.
